status: Read-only review preparation while Task149 CI runs; no adoption, implementation or live probe.

findings.finding: The user manager has user.delegate=1. The writable terminal scope lacks that marker; mode/access alone does not grant single-writer ownership. Do not reuse or mutate either existing hierarchy. A fresh dedicated delegated transient user service is a candidate, not a qualified executor.

memory_localevents makes memory.events local. A prospective profile must reject that mode or specify another complete mechanism before accepting parent-only event records; prefer a fixed absent-mode prerequisite.

The observed mount advertises memory_hugetlb_accounting. The draft instead assumes HugeTLB is excluded/prohibited. A reviewed profile can require pre-existing accounted mode explicitly, retaining documented pool/pre-existing-page limitations; never remount or configure a pool.
Retaining unknown event keys alone must not silently grant acceptance. Freeze recognized field semantics; new unreviewed fields require unavailable assessment rather than ignore-by-default.

systemd 259.5 user manager, writable delegated manager root and installed non-setuid bwrap are only capability clues. Direct birth, bounded ownership, default security, namespace isolation and retained terminal counters require an independent future proof.

Read final daemon/browser scope peaks before the final root peak, after all owned processes and collectors have exited. This supports parent >= child consistency without claiming simultaneous snapshots; unspecified or reversed order is unavailable.

The draft must not imply absence of all ambient pressure. Keep known low/sock_throttled events visible separately; reject high/max/oom/oom_kill/oom_group_kill and nonzero swap. New event keys require review. No imposed reclaim/limit changes is the intended restriction.

nextCandidate: Adopt a precise prospective contract only after resolving these scope/evidence ambiguities; implement a pure offline memory-receipt assessor first, never a full-flow acceptance shortcut.
